title: Coefficient-tower and identity coherence for normalized internal Hom
statement: Let M be normalized scalar and tensor-Hom models [def-sfb-scalar-hom-comparison-data], and let mu_a be a ScalarHomTensorComparison for each ring-sheaf map a. The explicitly constructed scalarHomCanonicalIso [def-sfb-scalar-hom-canonical-iso] satisfies coefficient-tower composition and identity coherence with exactly scalarHomRestrictionComp, scalarHomRestrictionId, scalarHomExtensionComp and scalarHomExtensionId. The left-adjoint comparisons are their unit-normalized leftAdjointUniq constructions; no extra compatibility hypothesis or flatness assumption is allowed. The full two equations, including all coefficient transports, are written verbatim in the Lean attachment.

proof.text: Use the tensor-coherence equations for the given normalized family. Form the composite tensor comparison F_b(mu_a) followed by mu_b; its natural isomorphism is obtained by whiskering and associators.

The canonical leftAdjointUniq map has the scalar-transpose compatibility required by the closed-Hom transport theorem. Apply that theorem to the composite scalar adjunction, the direct scalar adjunction, and the exact recorded restriction comparison. Tensor coherence supplies its tensor-compatibility hypothesis.

The generic composition calculation identifies the comparison for the composite adjunction with the two successive comparisons. Substitute this into the transport identity. For the identity, use the inverse leftAdjointUniq map, tensor identity coherence, and the identity closed-Hom comparison. Functoriality and associativity give precisely the two displayed equations.

lean.statement: theorem scalarInternalHomTowerCoherence (μ : ∀ {R S : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{max c v r}} (a : R ⟶ S), ScalarHomTensorComparison M a) : (∀ {R S T : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{max c v r}} (a : R ⟶ S) (b : S ⟶ T) (K : DerivedCategory (scalarModules J R)) (N : DerivedCategory (scalarModules J T)), (scalarHomCanonicalIso M (a ≫ b) (μ (a ≫ b))).hom.app (op K, N) ≫ (derivedInternalHomOfUniverses.{c, v, r, w} J R).map (Prod.mkHom (𝟙 (op K)) ((scalarHomRestrictionComp.{c, v, r, w} a b).hom.app N)) = (scalarHomRestrictionComp.{c, v, r, w} a b).hom.app ((derivedInternalHomOfUniverses.{c, v, r, w} J T).obj (op ((M.scalar (a ≫ b)).derived.obj K), N)) ≫ (scalarDerivedRestriction a).map ((scalarDerivedRestriction b).map ((derivedInternalHomOfUniverses.{c, v, r, w} J T).map (Prod.mkHom ((scalarHomExtensionComp M a b).hom.app K).op (𝟙 N)))) ≫ (scalarDerivedRestriction a).map ((scalarHomCanonicalIso M b (μ b)).hom.app (op ((M.scalar a).derived.obj K), N)) ≫ (scalarHomCanonicalIso M a (μ a)).hom.app (op K, (scalarDerivedRestriction b).obj N)) ∧ (∀ (R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{max c v r}) (K N : DerivedCategory (scalarModules J R)), (scalarHomCanonicalIso M (𝟙 R) (μ (𝟙 R))).hom.app (op K, N) ≫ (derivedInternalHomOfUniverses.{c, v, r, w} J R).map (Prod.mkHom (𝟙 (op K)) ((scalarHomRestrictionId.{c, v, r, w} R).hom.app N)) = (scalarHomRestrictionId.{c, v, r, w} R).hom.app ((derivedInternalHomOfUniverses.{c, v, r, w} J R).obj (op ((M.scalar (𝟙 R)).derived.obj K), N)) ≫ (derivedInternalHomOfUniverses.{c, v, r, w} J R).map (Prod.mkHom ((scalarHomExtensionId M R).inv.app K).op (𝟙 N)))
